study.title: LOPA – Hot DRI transfer conveyor and N2 fire protection (example)
study.unit: DRI plant – hot DRI transfer to EAF
study.team: A. Facilitator (LOPA), C. Process (process), E. Instrument (instrument / SIS), F. Fire (HSE / fire), D. Shift Supervisor (operations)
study.hazopTitle: HAZOP – Hot DRI transfer conveyor and N2 fire protection (example)
study.scope: Scenarios from the HAZOP LOPA study list for nodes N01 (hot DRI transfer conveyor) and N02 (N2 fire detection / inerting system). Illustrative values for training – not design data.

settings.basis: Typical example values – replace with the client's tolerable risk criteria before the study.

scenarios.cause: Conveyor, feeder or vibratory feeder stopped under load (belt tear, drive trip, chute blockage)
scenarios.consequence: Hot DRI stationary on the belt self-heats; belt fire spreads through the gallery to the transfer tower / DRI silo – potential fatality and extended outage

ie.basis: Plant trip records – about 6 per year (example; the same value as the fault tree example)

modifiers.desc: Fire develops from the stationary hot DRI
modifiers.basis: Fault tree example: a fire develops in 0.05 of stoppages under load – illustrative

modifiers.desc: Person present in the gallery when the fire spreads
modifiers.basis: Occupancy estimate: rounds about 10 % of the time – illustrative

ipls.name: XS-210 – N2 fire detection & inerting / extinguishing system
ipls.basis: Fault Tree & PFD Calculator example, gate G-002 PFDavg 0.0285

adj.evidence: Fault tree example G-002 (PFDavg 0.0285); proof-test and blow-through test records; cause & effect FP-N2-01
adj.conditions: Six-monthly function and blow-through test kept in the proof-test plan (FMECA)

ipls.name: Fire separation of the conveyor gallery (fire breaks / dampers)
ipls.basis: Engineering judgement – confirm against the fire-protection design basis

ipls.name: Emergency discharge chute operable without power (R-002)
ipls.basis: Proposed in the HAZOP (R-002) – assumed PFD 0.1

others: Restart / emergency discharge of hot DRI within safe time (procedure)
Manual fire fighting by the emergency response team
scenarios.notes: Gap remains after the proposed discharge chute – review the N2 system SIL (R-001) and inherently safer options.

fg-mvz2bks40eh7aw.note: PFD 0.0285 comes from a fault tree of the whole N2 system (FT G-002) – the detailed analysis the IPS guideline asks for

alarp.options: Environment, reputation and community: an enclosed fire-water collection system and a second N2 supply were considered
alarp.decision: Further risk reduction is not reasonably practicable – the risk is ALARP
alarp.justification: Small extra risk reduction (mainly asset) at high cost; the safety gap is addressed by R-001 and R-002

scenarios.result: SIL 1 needed (Safety, RRF 85.5); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1

scenarios.cause: Reduction / cooling upset – over-temperature DRI discharged onto the belt
scenarios.consequence: Belt damage or ignition; smouldering DRI carried to the EAF charging bin; conveyor fire

ie.basis: CCPS LOPA (2001), Table 5.1; CCPS Guidelines for Initiating Events and IPLs in LOPA (2015), Data Table 4.1

enabling.desc: Belt ignites when over-temperature DRI is discharged
enabling.basis: Engineering judgement – confirm the belt temperature rating (HAZOP R-004)

ipls.name: TSHH-202 – DRI discharge high-high temperature trip
ipls.basis: SIL 1 assumed – confirm by SIL verification

adj.evidence: Draft SRS for TSHH-202; separate sensor from TAH-202 to be confirmed

others: TAH-202 – High DRI temperature alarm (shares the sensor with TSHH-202: not independent)
XS-210 – N2 system (already credited in L-01, shares detection)

alarp.options: Second, diverse temperature trip; belt with a higher temperature rating

scenarios.result: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 (Asset, RRF 10)

scenarios.node: N02 – N2 fire detection, inerting & extinguishing system
scenarios.cause: Personnel enter the hood or gallery during or soon after an N2 release
scenarios.consequence: Asphyxiation in the conveyor enclosure – potential fatality

ie.desc: N2 release into the enclosure (demand or spurious)
ie.basis: Example: demands on the N2 system plus spurious releases – illustrative

enabling.desc: Entry into the enclosure while N2 is present

ipls.name: Confined-space entry permit with O2 test before entry
ipls.basis: Administrative IPL – credit only if audited and independent of the release warning; illustrative

ipls.name: Access door interlock with the N2 release (R-007)
ipls.basis: Proposed – SIL 2 door interlock assumed; illustrative

others: N2 release warning beacons and enclosure access lock-out
scenarios.result: SIL 3 needed (Safety, RRF 3.0E+3); with proposed IPLs: SIL 1 needed

log.ipl: XS-210 – N2 fire detection & inerting / extinguishing system
log.note: Six-monthly function and blow-through test kept in the proof-test plan (FMECA)

XS-210 – N2 fire detection & inerting /.setpoint: Stoppage under load > 2 min or TSHH / smoke detection → open XV-210A/B

TSHH-202 – DRI discharge high-high tempe.setpoint: To be set from the belt rating (HAZOP R-004)
TSHH-202 – DRI discharge high-high tempe.notes: Separate sensor from TAH-202 to be confirmed
